game.mcpConfig({ runId, verdictFile, testPlanFile })   // -> object to write as the Claude `--mcp-config` file
game.playtesterTools                                    // -> string[] for Claude `--allowedTools`
game.playtestPrompt(testPlan)                           // -> prompt for the playtester session
game.readVerdict(verdictFile, testPlan)                 // -> verdict (see above); unreported plan checks count as blocked
game.mockVerdict(testPlan, attempt)                     // mock only: attempt 1 fails the first check, attempt 2+ passes
```

**Who runs the playtester:** B's pipeline spawns the playtester as a normal Claude Code run (`claude -p --output-format stream-json --mcp-config <file> --allowedTools <playtesterTools>`) with `playtestPrompt(testPlan)`. That way Neatlogs traces it like every other session. In mock mode, B skips the session and uses `mockVerdict`.

**Events** (main → renderer through `emit`):

- `game:status`: the status object above.
- `game:log`: `{ line, level: 'info'|'warn'|'error', at }`, server console lines.
- `game:action`: `{ tool, args, result?, at }`, each MCP tool call the bot performs, for the GamePane overlay.

**IPC** (registered by `game.handlers(emit)`): `game:status`, `game:start`, `game:stop`, `game:command { command }`.

content.text:
Opening a chat now loads that mod onto a fresh world, and the live view has **Reset world** and **Run mod** buttons. I haven't run any of it against a real Paper server or an agent session. The build and the 28 existing tests pass, but they don't exercise this code. Nothing is committed.

**Why the world carried over:** each mod load restarted the server but kept the saved world on disk. The existing arena reset only covers a 20-block radius, so craters further out stayed. Every mod load now wipes the saved world first, so the new mod starts on untouched flat terrain.

**Opening a chat:** if the game is running and that chat's mod isn't the one on the server, it loads that mod on a fresh world. This is skipped while a build is running. If the game is stopped, **Start game** loads the chat's mod rather than whatever jar was last on disk.

**Mod identity:** the "which mod is loaded" check now compares the jar path instead of the plugin name. Two mods that share a plugin name could otherwise look identical and skip the reload.

**Reset world:** stops the server, wipes the world and restarts it with the same mod installed. That also clears plugin state like cooldowns. It takes a server restart, about 15–30 seconds by my guess.

**Run mod:** loads the mod first if needed, then a Sonnet agent drives the bot with the live-view tools:
- It resets the arena, uses the mod's test-plan setup, and shows the main behavior two or three times with pauses so you can follow.
- It doesn't judge pass or fail, and it runs outside the mod's repo so it isn't traced or checkpointed into the mod's history.
- A banner in the live view shows progress, then a one-sentence summary of what happened.
- The button turns into **Stop demo** while it runs. Creating a new mod, loading a mod or resetting the world also stops a running demo.

**Open questions:**
- Run mod costs Sonnet tokens each click, since the agent works out how to exercise the mod. A faster, free alternative is to have the spec agent write a fixed demo script. That wouldn't cover your existing mods, so I didn't do it.
- If you view chat B while chat A is building, B loads automatically when A finishes and replaces A's world. That matches "the live view shows the chat you're in", but say if you'd rather it stay on A.

The main changes are in `electron/lib/game/index.cjs`, `electron/lib/studio/index.cjs` and `src/components/game/GamePane.jsx`. Restart Benana before testing, since the main-process code changed. Do you want me to commit and push?
